subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` transcript archive convention and retention deletion behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration/purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: The source proves current behavior, but changing it affects shipped filenames, cleanup semantics, disk budgets, docs, memory/usage consumers, and downstream tooling, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with explicit purge
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and make physical purge an explicit documented retention policy.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave suffixes and cleanup semantics unchanged, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk pressure physically removes it.

options.title: Split policy from terminology
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 for naming/config clarity and track the no-physical-delete policy as a separate durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with explicit purge
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and make physical purge an explicit documented retention policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core storage and user-facing lifecycle decision, and CODEOWNERS/current-main evidence makes steipete the best available routing owner from the likely-owner set.
